summary: Unusually rigorous. All 76 quotations (on screen and spoken) trace to quotes.json, every shot's claim ids resolve, and spot checks of figures (AlexNet 15.3/26.2, the 3.88 stencil sum, softmax shares, 10 bits x 1.2M, n^2, 1/7 FLOPs, Nvidia -$589B, Pitts/McCulloch/Rosenblatt dates) all hold. Contested matters are flagged on screen (bedroom vs lab, Gebru's exit, backprop priority, IDSIA vs AlexNet, export-control views, Nobel 'physics?'). Remaining problems: one narrated line that implies DeepSeek concealed its chips, a 'Sources' card that points to a list that is not published, one quotation altered to British spelling, and a present-day act that names Anthropic's launch and research but never narrates Google's or Meta's LLM work. No prior rounds to check.

issues.problem: 'It left out the research, and the chips.' implies DeepSeek hid its hardware. The V3 report disclosed its 2,048 H800s and said in plain words that the $5.576M was a rental-price figure for the final run only, excluding prior research. The ~50,000-chip figure is an outside SemiAnalysis estimate (e13-cost-debate is marked contested; defenders note DeepSeek never claimed the whole programme cost $6M). This is the one place where the geopolitics act tilts against a Chinese lab.
issues.fix: Change to: 'That counted rented hours for the last run only: not the research before it, and not the hardware it owned.' Keep the on-screen 'EXCLUDES PRIOR RESEARCH · THE REPORT'S CAVEAT' tag and the attributed '~50,000 CHIPS (SEMIANALYSIS EST.)' tag.

issues.problem: ch15-s10 ends on 'SOURCES · published with the film', but nothing is published: public/generated/neural-net-history/ holds only manifest.json, film.vtt and audio, and the manifest has no sources key. So the film's one transparency promise is not kept, and the closing disclosure ('held to the same sources and standard') cannot be checked by a viewer.
issues.fix: At publish, generate a per-chapter sources page from script.json claim ids → claims.json sources and quotes.json source URLs, and link it from the manifest/shelf page. Or change the card to name where the sources actually live.

issues.problem: A verbatim quotation was altered. The 1998 Proc. IEEE abstract (LeCun, Bottou, Bengio & Haffner) reads 'reads several million checks per day'. The on-screen card, the L0603 caption (film.vtt line 511) and q-lecun-checks all say 'cheques', which looks like the British-spelling voice pass reaching inside quotation marks. The brief requires quotes to be verbatim.
issues.fix: Restore 'checks' in quotes.json q-lecun-checks, in the ch06-s02 quote card and in the L0603 caption text (the narration audio is unaffected). Add a guard so the British-spelling pass skips text inside quotation marks.

issues.problem: Lab balance in a film written by Anthropic's model. The 2023 'stampede' line names only OpenAI's GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude as co-equal launches. Google's Bard (e12-bard, 6 Feb 2023) and Meta's LLaMA (e12-llama-leak, which shows only as a date chip) are never narrated, and Gemini (e14-google) never appears. Meanwhile Anthropic also gets a founding scene, the film's only interpretability finding (ch15-s03) and its closing research quote (ch15-s08). Each item is accurate, but together they over-weight one lab relative to Google and Meta.
issues.fix: Rewrite L1219b along the lines of: 'Google rushed out Bard; Meta shared LLaMA with researchers, and its weights leaked within days; OpenAI's GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude arrived on the same March day.' (claims e12-bard, e12-llama-leak, e12-gpt4, e12-claude-launch). This also sets up the 'Qwen passes Llama' tag in ch14-s05, which right now refers to a model the viewer was never introduced to.

issues.problem: The only look inside a model in the present-day act is Anthropic's own paper, introduced as 'Anthropic's researchers looked inside...' and followed by 'Nobody told it to plan.' The closing 'one dark lantern' quote is also Anthropic's. This is accurate and well caveated ('simplified replacement model'), but interpretability is a field-wide effort.
issues.fix: Make it 'Researchers at Anthropic reported...' and add a short label or half-line saying that labs and universities are all doing this work (e.g. 'one of many such studies'). Alternatively, pair the ch15-s08 closing quote with a non-Anthropic source.

issues.problem: 'every seven months or so' is METR's March 2025 rate, presented as 'the candle of now' in October 2026. By the bible's own figures (Claude 3.7 Sonnet at ~1 h in Mar 2025; an early Mythos Preview at ≥16 h in May 2026), the recent pace is much faster, and METR warns that its suite cannot measure above ~16 h.
issues.fix: Date it: 'By one 2025 measure, every seven months or so...'. Or add the 2026 point to the on-screen label with METR's measurement caveat.

issues.problem: 'OpenAI kept those notes hidden', set directly against DeepSeek's 'recipe and weights open to all', frames OpenAI as secretive without its stated reason. 'Recipe ... open' also overstates R1: DeepSeek published the method and the weights (MIT), not its training data.
issues.fix: Use 'OpenAI hid those notes by design' (the claim's own wording) and 'its method and weights open to all'.

issues.problem: 'He would spend most of thirty-six years at the edge of the light' (paid off in L0832b) under-describes Hinton's standing. He co-authored the celebrated 1986 Nature paper, was elected FRS in 1998 and directed CIFAR NCAP from 2004. 'Edge of the light' is fair for the late-1990s neural-net winter, not for 1976–2012 as a whole.
issues.fix: Soften to 'He would spend much of the next thirty-six years near the edge of the light', or count only the winter years in L0832b.

issues.problem: 'The paper that put it out had Pitts's own name on it' credits the 1959 frog's-eye paper with ending the field-wide 'brain is a logic machine' belief. claims.json (e1-frog) supports only that the result disappointed Pitts about logic as the brain's language.
issues.fix: 'The paper that guttered it, for Pitts at least, had his own name on it.' Or keep the 16-year stub and attribute the end to the evidence piling up, not to one paper.

issues.problem: The read-in-order candle is 'lit in 1997' (L1002) and 'burned twenty years'. That ties the belief to the LSTM paper's date, but recurrent nets were the state of the art in language only from about 2013–14 (e10-rnn-belief supports 2017 dominance only), and sequential reading long predates 1997.
issues.fix: Light it at 'by 2014' with seq2seq, and change L1030 to 'The read-in-order candle burned only a few years at its height; the Transformer spread within two.' Or keep 1997 but say 'two decades of recurrent nets'.

issues.problem: Fairness to Minsky & Papert. The sentence quoted continues: they called it 'an important research problem to elucidate (or reject) our intuitive judgment' (e3-sterile). The film keeps only 'sterile', which makes the authors sound more dismissive than the text is. L0411 and the Papert 'Snow White' card balance this partly.
issues.fix: Add a few words: '...offered only what it called "our intuitive judgment that the extension is sterile", while calling it a problem worth settling.'

issues.problem: The 'might not hold forever — Gary Marcus, 2022' quote card appears in silence with no narration or label saying what 'might not hold' (the scaling laws). Out of context it reads as a free-floating jab.
issues.fix: Add a label such as 'scaling laws: "mere observations that might not hold forever" — Gary Marcus, 2022', or a half-line of narration.

best_moments: ch08-s13 'Fair credit: that was seven networks voting; one alone, nearer eighteen', followed by the IDSIA road-sign line. AlexNet gets its due and the contested priority is shown honestly.
ch05-s06: backprop's many inventors on one strip, then Hinton's own 'I have never claimed that I invented backpropagation.'
ch14 geopolitics: the 2017 plan 'named no rival'. BIS's military rationale and Mao Ning's reply are both quoted, three opposing tags on export controls, and the gap ends 'nobody agrees'.
ch12-s03: matched OpenAI and Anthropic mission cards, plus the FTX ledger line with 'not implicated'. Self-descriptions are labelled as such.
ch15-s05 'The labs, under the same light': Anthropic's Pentagon case shows the split courts, its $1.5B piracy settlement is stated plainly, and OpenAI's own 'warning shot' is quoted.
ch11-s08 Gebru card 'She says she was fired · Google says it accepted her resignation': both accounts, no verdict.
ch08-s04 worked stencil sum (3.88) and ch10-s06 attention toy (2,0,4,2 halved; about half to 'river'). Both are arithmetically exact.
